memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The LORD said to Moses, "Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites and say to them: 'This is what the LORD has commanded.'" - Lev 17:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice the audience. Aaron and his sons — the priests. And all the Israelites — everyone else.

Much of Leviticus so far has been addressed to the priests. Detailed instructions for those who handled the sacrifices, who wore the garments, who entered the holy places. The ordinary Israelite listened in but was not always the direct recipient.

Here God gathers everyone. Priests and farmers, leaders and labourers, the trained and the untrained. The same instruction, delivered to all of them together.

There is something in that worth holding on to. God does not have an inner circle who receive His real word and an outer circle who get a simplified version. His truth is public property among His people.

That conviction shaped the Reformation, when men risked their lives so ordinary people could read Scripture in their own language. It is why you can hold a Bible today. Paul told the Colossians to have his letter read publicly and passed to another church (Col 4:16). Luke wrote so that Theophilus might know the certainty of the things you have been taught (Luke 1:4).

You do not need a specialist to stand between you and God's Word. It was addressed to you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe you can genuinely understand Scripture yourself?
2. What stops you from reading God's Word more directly and regularly?
3. How can you help someone else gain confidence in reading it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your Word is not reserved for a select few but given to all Your people. Give me confidence and hunger to read it for myself. Amen.
